title: Convert an uncertain temperature without losing uncertainty
prompt: Convert a measured temperature of 20 ± 1 degrees Celsius to kelvin. The ±1 is a standard uncertainty. Also convert the two endpoints 19 and 21 degrees Celsius. Explain how the uncertainty changes and state any assumptions. Do not edit files.
rubric: The response reports 293.15 K with standard uncertainty 1 K.
The endpoints are 292.15 K and 294.15 K, and the offset is applied to each endpoint.
It applies the offset to the temperature and not to the uncertainty interval.
It does not invent an expanded uncertainty or coverage probability.
acceptance: The converted measurement preserves the stated standard uncertainty.
